events.title: Altair 8800 released
events.summary: MITS put the Altair 8800 on the January 1975 cover of Popular Electronics — the machine that sparked the personal computer revolution, with working kits shipping in early 1975.
events.about: The Altair was a bare-bones Intel 8080 box with switches and blinking lights — no keyboard, no monitor. Hobbyists ordered thousands of kits; Bill Gates and Paul Allen wrote Altair BASIC for it and founded Microsoft. Every garage-startup PC narrative starts here: cheap hardware + software you could sell.

narrative.whyChosen: The Altair proved a market existed for personal microcomputers beyond mainframes and minis.
narrative.whyImportant: It launched the hobbyist-to-industry pipeline that produced Apple, Microsoft, and the IBM PC ecosystem.
narrative.problemSolved: Enthusiasts wanted an affordable computer they could own, extend, and program at home.
